quotes.text: Paul, an apostle—not from men nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: The opening words of the letter, stressing that his apostleship came directly from Christ and God, not from any human authority.

quotes.text: I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting him who called you in the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Skipping his usual thanksgiving, Paul goes straight to rebuking the Galatians for turning to another gospel.

quotes.text: But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be accursed.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Warning the Galatians against the different gospel being taught by those troubling them; he repeats the curse in the next verse.

quotes.text: If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Defending himself against the charge that he softened the gospel to win human approval.

quotes.text: For I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it, but I received it through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Explaining the source of his gospel before recounting his life story.

quotes.text: how I persecuted the church of God violently and tried to destroy it
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Recalling his former life in Judaism, before God called him.

quotes.text: In what I am writing to you, before God, I do not lie!
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: An oath in the middle of describing his first Jerusalem visit, when he saw only Cephas and James.

quotes.text: He who used to persecute us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.
quotes.speaker: The churches of Judea (what they kept hearing about Paul)
quotes.context: While Paul was in Syria and Cilicia, still unknown in person to the Judean churches; they glorified God because of him.

quotes.text: to them we did not yield in submission even for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel might be preserved for you
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: About the false brothers who slipped in to spy out their freedom during his second Jerusalem visit, when Titus was not forced to be circumcised.

quotes.text: what they were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: An aside about the leaders in Jerusalem who "seemed to be influential"; they added nothing to his gospel.

quotes.text: Only, they asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: The one request James, Cephas and John made when they gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship.

quotes.text: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Introducing the incident at Antioch where Peter (Cephas) withdrew from eating with Gentile believers.

quotes.text: If you, though a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you force the Gentiles to live like Jews?
quotes.speaker: Paul, to Cephas (Peter) "before them all"
quotes.context: At Antioch, after Peter drew back from eating with the Gentiles when men came from James, and even Barnabas was led astray. (Peter himself has no recorded words in Galatians.)

quotes.text: a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Continuing from his rebuke of Peter at Antioch: even Jews by birth know this.

quotes.text: I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Explaining that through the law he died to the law so that he might live to God.

quotes.text: for if righteousness were through the law, then Christ died for no purpose
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: The conclusion of his argument after the Antioch episode: he does not nullify the grace of God.

quotes.text: O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you?
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Opening his doctrinal argument: Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified before their eyes.

quotes.text: Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being perfected by the flesh?
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Asking whether they received the Spirit by works of the law or by hearing with faith.

quotes.text: believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness
quotes.speaker: Scripture, about Abraham
quotes.context: Paul cites Abraham as proof that righteousness comes by faith: those of faith are the sons of Abraham.

quotes.text: In you shall all the nations be blessed.
quotes.speaker: God, speaking to Abraham (the Scripture "preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham")
quotes.context: Paul says the Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith.

quotes.text: Cursed be everyone who does not abide by all things written in the Book of the Law, and do them.
quotes.speaker: Moses, in the curses of the Law
quotes.context: Paul argues that all who rely on works of the law are under a curse.

quotes.text: The righteous shall live by faith.
quotes.speaker: God, answering the prophet Habakkuk
quotes.context: Paul shows that no one is justified before God by the law.

quotes.text: The one who does them shall live by them.
quotes.speaker: God, giving the law through Moses
quotes.context: Paul contrasts the law with faith: the law is not of faith.

quotes.text: Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree
quotes.speaker: Moses, in the Law
quotes.context: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us.

quotes.text: And to your offspring
quotes.speaker: God, promising to Abraham
quotes.context: Paul notes the promise says "offspring," not "offsprings," referring to one: Christ.

quotes.text: the law, which came 430 years afterward, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Using the human example of a ratified covenant to show that the law cannot cancel the promise to Abraham.

quotes.text: Why then the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise had been made
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Answering the obvious objection after arguing that the inheritance comes by promise, not by law.

quotes.text: So then, the law was our guardian until Christ came, in order that we might be justified by faith.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Describing the law as a temporary guardian; now that faith has come we are no longer under it.

quotes.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is no male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: All who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ and are sons of God through faith.

quotes.text: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Following the illustration of the heir who is still a child, under guardians until the date set by his father.

quotes.text: Abba! Father!
quotes.speaker: The Spirit of God's Son, crying in our hearts
quotes.context: Because believers are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into their hearts.

quotes.text: You observe days and months and seasons and years!
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Rebuking the Galatians for turning back to the weak and worthless elementary principles of the world.

quotes.text: if possible, you would have gouged out your eyes and given them to me
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Remembering how warmly they welcomed him when he first preached to them because of a bodily ailment.

quotes.text: Have I then become your enemy by telling you the truth?
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Contrasting their first welcome with their present attitude toward him.

quotes.text: my little children, for whom I am again in the anguish of childbirth until Christ is formed in you!
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: A tender personal appeal; he is perplexed about them and wishes he could be present.

quotes.text: Rejoice, O barren one who does not bear; break forth and cry aloud, you who are not in labor!
quotes.speaker: The prophet Isaiah
quotes.context: Paul applies it to the free "Jerusalem above," our mother, in his allegory of Hagar and Sarah.

quotes.text: Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman.
quotes.speaker: Sarah, demanding that Abraham send away Hagar and Ishmael
quotes.context: Paul quotes it as "the Scripture" to conclude the Hagar and Sarah allegory: we are children of the free woman.

quotes.text: For freedom Christ has set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: The turn from argument to application, right after the allegory of the slave woman and the free woman.

quotes.text: You are severed from Christ, you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Warning those considering circumcision that it obligates them to keep the whole law.

quotes.text: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only faith working through love.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Part of his warning against accepting circumcision.

quotes.text: You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth?
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Lamenting the influence of the agitators on the Galatians.

quotes.text: A little leaven leavens the whole lump.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: A proverb warning how the false teaching spreads through the whole church.

quotes.text: I wish those who unsettle you would emasculate themselves!
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: A sharp outburst against those insisting the Galatians be circumcised.

quotes.text: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
quotes.speaker: God, giving the law through Moses
quotes.context: Paul says the whole law is fulfilled in this one word, so use freedom to serve one another through love.

quotes.text: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Explaining how to live in freedom without giving opportunity to the flesh.

quotes.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Contrasted with the works of the flesh listed just before.

quotes.text: If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Following the list of the fruit of the Spirit: those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh.

quotes.text: Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Instructions on restoring a brother caught in transgression in a spirit of gentleness.

quotes.text: Do not be deceived: God is not mocked, for whatever one sows, that will he also reap.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Teaching on sharing with teachers and sowing to the Spirit rather than to the flesh.

quotes.text: And let us not grow weary of doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Encouragement to keep sowing to the Spirit and do good to everyone.

quotes.text: See with what large letters I am writing to you with my own hand.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Taking the pen himself for the closing section of the letter.

quotes.text: But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Contrasted with the circumcision party, who want to boast in the Galatians' flesh.

quotes.text: For neither circumcision counts for anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: The closing summary of the letter, written in his own hand.

quotes.text: From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.
quotes.speaker: Paul
quotes.context: Paul's final words before the benediction, pointing to the scars of his sufferings.

verses.text: who gave himself for our sins to deliver us from the [[present evil age]], according to the will of our God and Father,
I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting him who called you in the grace of Christ and are turning to a [[different gospel]]—
But even if we or an [[angel from heaven]] should preach to you a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be [[accursed]].
For am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God? Or am I trying to please man? If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a [[servant of Christ]].
For I would have you know, brothers, that the gospel that was preached by me is not [[man's gospel]].
For I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it, but I received it through a [[revelation]] of Jesus Christ.
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into [[Arabia]], and returned again to [[Damascus]].
Then after [[three years]] I went up to Jerusalem to visit [[Cephas]] and remained with him [[fifteen days]].
But I saw none of the other apostles except [[James]] the Lord's brother.
Then after [[fourteen years]] I went up again to Jerusalem with [[Barnabas]], taking [[Titus]] along with me.

and when James and Cephas and John, who seemed to be [[pillars]], perceived the grace that was given to me, they gave the [[right hand of fellowship]] to Barnabas and me, that we should go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.
Only, they asked us to [[remember the poor]], the very thing I was eager to do.
But when Cephas came to [[Antioch]], I opposed him [[to his face]], because he stood condemned.

yet we know that a person is not justified by [[works of the law]] but through [[faith in Jesus Christ]], so we also have believed in Christ Jesus, in order to be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.
For through the law I [[died to the law]], so that I might live to God.

I have been [[crucified with Christ]]. It is no longer I who live, but [[Christ who lives in me]]. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
I do not nullify the grace of God, for if righteousness were through the law, then Christ died for [[no purpose]].
O [[foolish Galatians]]! Who has [[bewitched]] you? It was before your eyes that Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified.
Let me ask you only this: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law or by [[hearing with faith]]?
Are you so foolish? Having begun by the [[Spirit]], are you now being perfected by the [[flesh]]?
just as Abraham “believed God, and it was [[counted to him as righteousness]]”?
Know then that it is those of faith who are the [[sons of Abraham]].
And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham, saying, “In you shall [[all the nations]] be blessed.”
Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, for “[[The righteous shall live by faith]].”
Christ redeemed us from the [[curse of the law]] by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who is [[hanged on a tree]]”—
so that in Christ Jesus the [[blessing of Abraham]] might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the [[promised Spirit]] through faith.
Now the promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say, “And to offsprings,” referring to many, but referring to one, “And to your offspring,” [[who is Christ]].
This is what I mean: the law, which came [[430 years]] afterward, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to make the promise void.
Why then the law? It was added [[because of transgressions]], until the offspring should come to whom the promise had been made, and it was put in place through [[angels]] by an intermediary.
So then, the law was our [[guardian]] until Christ came, in order that we might be justified by faith.
for in Christ Jesus you are all [[sons of God]], through faith.
For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have [[put on Christ]].
There is neither [[Jew nor Greek]], there is neither [[slave nor free]], there is no [[male and female]], for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you are Christ's, then you are [[Abraham's offspring]], [[heirs]] according to promise.
But when the [[fullness of time]] had come, God sent forth his Son, [[born of woman]], born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive [[adoption as sons]].
And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “[[Abba! Father!]]”
So you are no longer a slave, but a son, and if a son, then [[an heir through God]].

But now that you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, how can you turn back again to the weak and worthless [[elementary principles]] of the world, whose slaves you want to be once more?
You know it was because of a [[bodily ailment]] that I preached the gospel to you at first,
my little children, for whom I am again in the [[anguish of childbirth]] until [[Christ is formed in you]]!
Now this may be interpreted allegorically: these women are [[two covenants]]. One is from [[Mount Sinai]], bearing children for slavery; she is [[Hagar]].
But the [[Jerusalem above]] is free, and she is our mother.
Now you, brothers, like [[Isaac]], are [[children of promise]].
For [[freedom]] Christ has set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not submit again to a [[yoke of slavery]].
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only [[faith working through love]].
A little [[leaven]] leavens the whole lump.
For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an [[opportunity for the flesh]], but through love [[serve one another]].
For the whole law is fulfilled in [[one word]]: “You shall [[love your neighbor as yourself]].”
But I say, [[walk by the Spirit]], and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are [[opposed to each other]], to keep you from doing the things you want to do.
But if you are [[led by the Spirit]], you are not under the law.
But the fruit of the Spirit is [[love]], [[joy]], [[peace]], [[patience]], [[kindness]], [[goodness]], [[faithfulness]], [[gentleness]], [[self-control]]; against such things there is no law.
And those who belong to Christ Jesus have [[crucified the flesh]] with its passions and desires.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also [[keep in step]] with the Spirit.
Brothers, if anyone is caught in any transgression, you who are spiritual should [[restore him]] in a [[spirit of gentleness]]. Keep watch on yourself, lest you too be tempted.
Bear one another's [[burdens]], and so fulfill the [[law of Christ]].
For each will have to bear [[his own load]].
Do not be deceived: God is not [[mocked]], for whatever one [[sows]], that will he also [[reap]].
For the one who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap [[corruption]], but the one who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap [[eternal life]].
And let us not [[grow weary]] of doing good, for in [[due season]] we will reap, if we do not give up.
So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those who are of the [[household of faith]].
See with what [[large letters]] I am writing to you with my own hand.
But far be it from me to boast except in [[the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ]], by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For neither circumcision counts for anything, nor uncircumcision, but a [[new creation]].
From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the [[marks of Jesus]].

names.name: Paul
names.note: Author of the letter; former persecutor of the church, called by grace to preach Christ among the Gentiles.

names.name: Cephas (Peter)
names.note: Apostle to the circumcised; Paul stayed with him fifteen days, and later opposed him at Antioch for withdrawing from Gentiles.

names.name: James
names.note: The Lord's brother, a 'pillar' of the Jerusalem church; 'certain men came from James' to Antioch.

names.name: John
names.note: One of the three 'pillars' who gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship.

names.name: Barnabas
names.note: Went up to Jerusalem with Paul; at Antioch he too was 'led astray' by the hypocrisy.

names.name: Titus
names.note: A Greek who went with Paul to Jerusalem and was not forced to be circumcised.

names.name: Jesus Christ
names.note: Gave himself for our sins; the one 'offspring' of Abraham; Paul boasts only in his cross.

names.name: Abraham
names.note: Believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness; those of faith are his sons and offspring.

names.name: Hagar
names.note: The slave woman; in Paul's allegory she is Mount Sinai and the present Jerusalem, bearing children for slavery.

names.name: Sarah
names.note: The free woman (not named in Galatians), mother of the child of promise; pictures the Jerusalem above.

names.name: Isaac
names.note: Abraham's son by the free woman, born through promise; believers are children of promise like him.

names.name: Ishmael
names.note: Abraham's son by the slave woman (not named in Galatians), born according to the flesh; he persecuted the child of the Spirit.

names.name: Galatia
names.note: The region whose churches Paul addresses ("O foolish Galatians!").

names.name: Jerusalem
names.note: Paul visited after three years and again after fourteen; the "present Jerusalem" is in slavery, but the "Jerusalem above" is free.

names.name: Antioch
names.note: Where Paul opposed Cephas to his face over withdrawing from table fellowship with Gentiles.

names.name: Arabia
names.note: Where Paul went right after his call, instead of going up to Jerusalem; Mount Sinai is in Arabia.

names.name: Damascus
names.note: Paul returned there from Arabia.

names.name: Mount Sinai
names.note: Where the law was given; in the allegory it is Hagar, bearing children for slavery.

names.name: Syria and Cilicia
names.note: Regions where Paul went after his first Jerusalem visit.

names.name: Judea
names.note: Its churches did not know Paul by face but glorified God because of him.

events.event: Paul persecutes the church of God violently
God reveals his Son to Paul to preach among the Gentiles
Paul goes away into Arabia and returns to Damascus
After three years Paul visits Cephas in Jerusalem for fifteen days
Paul goes into the regions of Syria and Cilicia
After fourteen years Paul goes up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus
Titus is not forced to be circumcised; false brothers resisted
James, Cephas and John give Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship
Cephas withdraws from eating with Gentiles at Antioch
Paul rebukes Cephas before them all
Paul first preaches to the Galatians because of a bodily ailment
Abraham has two sons, one by a slave woman and one by a free woman
Paul writes the closing with large letters in his own hand
